description:
FILED s543a (Opus; drafted 2026-11-16, filed 2026-11-21 with the bench) -- PERF, sized, NOT built.  Line tracking is ON by default since s543a (the USER, s543): every lowered statement writes `(p-line N)` (one store to a defglobal: ~0.25 ns measured s473c, ~0.6 ns per iteration in the feread loop below; ir-spec 6.3b).  The cost it leaves on the bench is concentrated where a statement is a few ns: the counting loops.  Two narrowings remove stores whose value nobody can read; both keep every location perl would report.

MEASURED (s543a full bench, K=5, interleaved, base c5f618f2 vs the s543a tree, each side its own pl2cl + runtime; the noise band base-vs-base is in docs/caller-implementation.md "What it costs"):
  (scratch/s543a/bench-noise.log + bench-tree.log of the s543a worktree, 2026-11-21 14:41-14:56, load 0.7-1.8; cost = tree/base - 1, > 0 = slower; the base-vs-base band of the same box: rows < 0.1 s -6.8 .. +9.6 %, rows >= 0.1 s -3.8 .. +4.9 %; scratch/s543a/bench-cmp.pl)
  * OUTSIDE the band, a store in a few-ns loop body (this task's target): feread +17.1 % (0.1047 -> 0.1226 s: `for my $x (@a) { $s += $x }`, one (p-line 1) per inner iteration of a ~3.5 ns body, ~0.6 ns per store; SAME-LINE: the foreach statement wrote line 1 just before), feread2 +15.7 % (0.1099 -> 0.1272), feread3 +15.8 % (0.1139 -> 0.1319), collatz +7.2 % (0.3199 -> 0.3428: two stores per inner while iteration, `$m = ...; $c++`, same line).
  * The counting loops, consistently slower but INSIDE the short-row band: intloop+= +6.4 % (0.0202 -> 0.0215), intloop= +4.9 % (0.0185 -> 0.0194), cfor +4.1 % (0.0244 -> 0.0254), arith +3.1 % (0.0360 -> 0.0371); also pushloc +6.3 %, boolif +5.9 %, shiftq +5.5 %, grepcnt +5.3 %.
  * OUTSIDE, per-call rows, NOT attributed (the stores alone are ~0.5 ns each, the difference is ~15 ns per iteration): emptysub +8.1 % (0.3687 -> 0.3984), methinh +5.2 % (0.3288 -> 0.3458).  Rows FASTER with no possible emission gain -- blessnew -5.6 %, splitstrre -4.6 %, blessdes -4.2 % (and the 10-16 ms rows accumread -14.0 %, symref -6.9 %) -- say the long rows' real run-to-run spread is about +-6 %, wider than the one-sample band.
  * Over the 77 rows: median +0.8 %, geomean +1.1 % (the noise run's geomean +0.6 %).

THE CENSUS (scratch/s543a/census.pl over the s543a emission of the 2,053-file wide list -- perl-tests, everyday, lib, perl's t/, core lib, the board dists):
  * (p-line N) forms: 198,613.
  * SAME-LINE stores -- the (p-line) just before it in document order wrote the same N: 13,617 = 6.9 % (an upper estimate; the corpus 9.4 %, the everyday programs 75.7 %: compact programs put many statements on one line).  A loop body or a block on the statement's own line rewrites the line the statement already wrote (`(p-foreach-range-raw ($_ 1 $n) (p-line 3) (p-unshift @a $_))` after `(p-line 3)`), and so does each statement of `f(); g(); h();`.  Dead when nothing between the two stores can leave the register at another value: a sub call restores it on a normal return (p-sub-frame's p-loc-save), so the only writer is a NON-LOCAL exit out of a callee (a dynamic `next`/`last` from a called sub -- dyn-loop-exit -- skips the callee's restore).  Rule: drop the store when the previous store on the straight path wrote the same N and no form between them can exit non-locally into this block (no call inside a dyn-exit loop; conservative: no call at all in the loop body).
  * RAW-ONLY statements -- the store precedes a statement made only of raw forms that cannot raise or call: 669 = 0.3 % (corpus 28, everyday 11).  The closed list of heads I would trust: `setf` of a raw slot, `p-incf-raw`, `p-decf-raw`, and inside them only `p-+ p-- p-* p-< p-> p-<= p->= p-== p-!= p-<=>` over `$raw-slot`s and numeric literals (the raw-numeric verdict proves the operands are numbers, so no overload, tie or string coercion can call user code).  Division and modulus are NOT on it: `Illegal division by zero` / `Illegal modulus zero` is exactly the runtime-raised die the register exists for; `p-**`, `int`, string ops and any call stay off it too.  Few statements qualify, but they are the hot ones: intloop= (`$s = $s + $_`), cfor (`$t = $t + $i` and the `$i++` step), intloop+= (`$u += $_`).
  * The two rules overlap on exactly the counting loops: there the body's store is BOTH same-line and raw-only.

EXPECTED GAIN: the counting-loop rows back to the base (they pay one store per iteration and nothing else changed); the macro rows unchanged (inside the band before and after).  Text: the same-line rule removes up to ~7 % of the stores (~1.5 % of the emitted text on Calc.pm-like code, measure); the raw-only rule ~0.3 %.

NOT TO BUILD AS: an emission that decides from TEXT; both rules belong in Parser2's `_lower_block` (the ONE emission site, ir-spec 6.3b) as facts of the lowered tree (the raw verdicts are already there).  Bar: the die-location / caller-fidelity rows unchanged, ir-conform 0 / 0, the bench rows above.
subject: PERF: line tracking costs one store per statement on the bench loops (feread +16..17 %, collatz +7 %) -- drop the dead stores: a same-line store and a store before a raw-only statement (sized, not built)
triage_reason: speed: the per-statement location store on the counting loops (outside the claim; sized, not built)
